title: The spectral Erdős book theorem: sharp bounds and stability
summary: The booksize $\mathrm{bk}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the largest number of triangles sharing a common edge. A classical theorem of Edwards, conjectured by Bollobás and Erdős, states that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $e(G)>e(T_{n,2})$ has booksize greater than $n/6$. Zhai and Lin [J. Graph Theory 102 (2023) 502--520] asked whether the same conclusion holds under the spectral condition $λ(G)>λ(T_{n,2})$, where $λ(G)$ is the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix.
